NB-aware: I use awareness to mean bare, non-reflective appearance: blue is just blue. Consciousness is awareness reflecting back on itself: “I’m blue!” Pāli doesn’t give me separate nouns for this distinction, but DN 11 and MN 49 describe viññāṇaṃ anidassanaṃ anantaṃ sabbato pabhaṃ – non-manifesting awareness, without end and luminous all around – where the elements and mind-and-body (nāmarūpa, often mistranslated as name-and-form) find no footing. The texts distinguish that from ordinary sense-consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) established when one thing perceives another.
NB-mn89note:
The standard isn’t the non-stop, 24/7 bliss that Soh claimed, which is false. In AN 11.12, a noble disciple can reach ease through recollection, so ease is something a disciple reaches through practice, not a permanent state they’re stuck in. In MN 75, the Buddha says that what ordinary people perceive as sensual pleasure, he felt as pain. So enlightenment isn’t a simple bliss switch.

Does the Dhamma now feel intuitively coherent rather than merely conceptual?
NB-lucid: The lucid-dream comparison from earlier also shapes how I understand the seven-life limit said to be had by the stream-enterer. Once the dream is known as a dream, it becomes naturally difficult to remain stuck in it, similar to how hard it is to be absorbed in a movie when the lights go on and you remember you’re in a theater. If you’ve ever had a lucid dream, you know what I’m talking about.
NB-attribute: I used to attribute “life is like a dream” directly to the historical Buddha, until I found out the famous stanza I loved comes from the much later Mahāyāna Diamond Sutra, which puts some words in his mouth. The early Pāli texts do give us some very similar kind of symbolism, though. SN 22.95 shows us how form is empty and always transforming, like foam, fleeting feeling is compared to a bubble, perception is only a mirage, and consciousness is basically the best magic trick. And Dhammapada 170 asks us to see the world as a bubble and mirage, so if you put it all together, you can certainly imagine that the basic idea of life being like a dream was originally intended.
